correctness.rationale: Completing squares in the two mixed terms yields conjugate phases ±π(b−a)Tν/(a+b); the diagonal terms give the two positive real envelopes in (1). Dividing by the nonvanishing cross amplitude preserves analytic multiplicities. The envelope exponents vanish at aT and bT respectively and change by ∓2βK and ±2βK, up to O(T⁻²), at the corresponding offsets ±K/T. Monotonicity gives the uniform inner and outer bounds. On each negative lobe intersected with the enlarged wedge the normalized function has strictly positive second derivative: ν≥aT/2 makes even the decreasing Gaussian term strictly convex for large T. An interior lobe has positive endpoints and negative midpoint, hence two simple roots; a clipped lobe has at most two in the wedge counted with multiplicity (a stationary zero has order two). Negative lobes have spacing 2(a+b)/[(b−a)T], so the two edge strips change the count by O(1). For any fixed T>0, including short delays, the increasing envelope summand tends to infinity as ν→∞; analyticity and h_T(0)>0 imply finitely many zeros in the remaining compact interval. At zero delay the cosine is one; if a=b or c=0 the pulse is a single Gaussian. The archived finite numerical checks were inspected, not rerun, and are not needed to certify multiplicities or the unbounded-delay count.
residual_risks: Constants are for fixed unequal widths and fixed c>0; the numerical enumeration is not a certificate near finite-delay tangencies.

value.rationale: The simplest positive superposition of unequal widths changes the one-Gaussian zero-free behavior to a growing, sharply located population of real nulls. The exact count to O(1), with simple crossings in the bulk and only boundedly many edge exceptions, determines more than existence or growth order; it explains which parameter controls bulk null density and why amplitude imbalance moves only the edges at fixed parameters.
residual_risks: No inference about arbitrary mixtures, complex roots, or uniformity in the coalescing-width and vanishing-amplitude limits.
